head: bb300ecbd87fa6a8a449118fb45cadac2ce4a6eb
title: Avoid broadcasted GIST cosine matrices during training
body:
## Change

Compute the default GIST cosine-similarity matrix by normalizing each embedding once and multiplying the two matrices. GISTEmbedLoss and CachedGISTEmbedLoss currently broadcast to a batch-by-batch-by-dimension tensor, including tensors retained for backward. The shared helper removes that expansion.

The optimized path handles matching float32/float64 inputs on CPU/CUDA. Other dtypes, custom similarity modules and non-default dimensions retain their existing path. Autocast is disabled for the matrix product to preserve float32 inputs. The norm clamp remains outside autograd, matching CosineSimilarity's derivative for norms below eps.

This was identified through code analysis and reproduced through the public loss classes with precomputed embeddings. It is separate from the positive/self-pair masking fix in #4284 and distributed gathering in #4223.

## Validation

[Exact-base comparison on PyTorch 2.6.0 and 2.14.1](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43912070038) checks base `9ac7fdb4` and candidate `bb300ecb`:

- **88 passed** on both baseline and candidate in each environment, including existing GIST/CachedGIST tests, full loss values and embedding gradients, rectangular/non-contiguous inputs, both margin strategies, tiny norms, configured eps, mixed/low-precision fallbacks, custom similarity classes and CPU autocast.
- Independent native float64 cosine references cover input scales 1e-10, 1 and 1e8. For the tiny-scale float32 diagnostic, gradient norm-relative errors against float64 were 2.7e-8 to 9.2e-8 for the candidate across both PyTorch versions; native float32 errors were 5.4e-8 to 9.7e-8. The test checks normwise accuracy rather than relative error of an individual cancellation-prone coordinate.
- Every repository pre-commit hook and `git diff --check` passes in both environments.

The [reproducible benchmark](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/3cde827942f143df82caada3c1a966cca19d2fbc/.validation/st-gist-cosine-benchmark.py) measures complete loss forward/backward operations with fixed precomputed embeddings, one CPU thread, two warmups and seven timed runs. Losses and gradients are checked against the baseline.

| PyTorch 2.14.1 case | Before median | After median | Ratio | Saved tensor storage before / after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GIST, batch 64, dimension 384 | 66.64 ms | 1.47 ms | 45.25× | 96.86 / 1.87 MiB |
| GIST, batch 128, dimension 768 | 1824.78 ms | 7.85 ms | 232.32× | 771.44 / 7.46 MiB |
| CachedGIST, batch 128, dimension 384, mini-batch 32 | 330.83 ms | 6.69 ms | 49.48× | 193.88 / 4.65 MiB |

The corresponding PyTorch 2.6.0 timing ratios were 47.25×, 233.22× and 48.72×. Saved storage means unique tensor storage retained for autograd, not peak process memory. These component measurements exclude the encoder and cached embedding replay; GPU performance was not measured.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped with investigation, implementation, numerical validation and this description.
